newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: UN Council asks Zairean rebels to help refugees.
newsitem.headline: UN Council asks Zairean rebels to help refugees.

text.p: With Rwandan refugees dying of malnutrition and disease, the United Nations Security Council late on Friday called on Zaire's rebel leader Laurent Kabila to let aid agencies help refugees to return home.

The 15-member body "strongly" urged all parties, in particular Kabila's Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo/Zaire, to allow the agencies to aid the refugees and other civilians caught in Zaire's civil war.

It said the rebels should "cooperate fully" with repatriation plans drawn up by the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees, who has reported that at least 120 Rwandan Hutu refugees were dying each day in two camps south of the rebel-held city of Kisangani in eastern Zaire.
The council's relatively mildly worded appeal was read by its current president, Portuguese ambassador Antonio Monteiro, at a formal meeting.
It also said Rwanda should facilitate the return of the refugees, although it did not spell out complaints about Rwanda's cooperation in the repatriation process.
The rebels are fighting to get rid of Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko and have captured a quarter of the country.
Although they would like to see Rwandan refugees leave, they will not allow them to board planes from the city of Kisangani in eastern Zaire.

Instead they want them to walk hundreds of miles overland back to Rwanda, arguing that they include militia responsible for the 1994 massacre of Tutsis in Rwanda. U.N. officials say the vast majority are innocent.

The council noted in its statement that Kabila had extended some cooperation in allowing aid groups to reach refugees south of Kisangani. State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said the rebels on Friday were allowing some displaced Zairians to be airlifted from Kisangani to Goma.
"We need permission to bring out the Rwandan citizens, and the other African citizens who are affected by this," he said.

Chief U.N. spokesman Fred Eckhard on Thursday said the U.N. refugee agency had asked Kabila in writing on March 29 for permission to fly out thousands of seriously ill people, but no answer had been received.

"So we call on Mr. Kabila to let the relief organisations do their work and to stop the killing of these people -- which is what it is -- and which has been going on for the last several months," he said.

The U.N. aid agencies on Friday, joined by the European Union, issued an appeal directed at representatives of the Zairean government and the rebels before their planned peace talks in South Africa this weekend.

It was signed by Emma Bonino, the EU commissioner for humanitarian affairs; Sadako Ogata, the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees; Carol Bellamy, head of the United Nations children's fund UNICEF, and by an official of the World Food Programme on behalf of its director, Catherine Bertini.
"We have witnessed the plight of the refugees ourselves," they said in a statement. "We are now trying to help them and prepare for repatriation."

"Aid agencies should be able to work without any restrictions to save many thousands of refugees and displaced persons who are exhausted after months of roaming desperately through the jungle and whose lives are currently hanging by a thread," they added.
